evidence: Android crash buffer backtrace terminating in nativePushReport
persisted flight record showing a high-volume FILE stream followed by transport close, reopen, and handshake attempt

rootCause.statement: The high-volume capture read intentionally refreshed the USB session. Cancellation of the queued Android UsbRequest ring produced a residual one-byte completion. The shared body-only report normalizer accepted any nonempty read, after which TransportRuntime::push_report indexed report[2]. The resulting Rust bounds panic crossed an extern system JNI boundary and aborted the Android process.

changes: Reject body-only reports shorter than the two-byte HID length and flags header in shared Rust.
Reject teardown-shortened reports in the Android adapter before JNI.
Catch unexpected nativePushReport panics and convert them to the Java error path instead of unwinding across JNI.
Exercise every native read length from zero through twice the logical report size in a regression test.
